To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the advent of a big data era is impacting the role and function of managers and that business schools and higher educational institutions must evolve to better tackle educational challenges associated with big data analytics (BDADS) training.
the advent of a new era in which business is driven by big data analytics and the associated data science is a game-changer that will impact all functions of organizations.
the advent of the big data era has triggered the emergence of a new type of decision makers: manager-scientists whose skills are at the crossroad between data management, analytics and business.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to prepare managers to deal with the data-driven business world.
the educational challenges triggered in the wake of the digital revolution.
the educational challenges triggered in the business world by the advent of a big data-driven era and the implications of these challenges for business education.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data-driven era has brought about a paradigm shift in management and business.
the current business education model is inadequate to prepare future decision makers and business leaders for the new data driven business era.
the data-driven business world necessitates a new breed of manager-scientists, who will need to be trained in a new type of business schools.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are facing a new era of business education that is more multidisciplinary and more experiential.
business education must become more interdisciplinary and that the function of managers is evolving into a multidisciplinary role that shall encompass data science skills.
we are in need of manager-scientists.
The main takeaway from our work is that
managers must be trained to become “manager-scientists” who shall possess skills that are both analytical and business oriented.
the data-driven business world is here to stay.
business schools must not only focus on training the next generation of data scientists.
